steps.title: Get the transcript
do: Find the transcript for this client and the meeting date Paul gave. Try the three routes IN THIS ORDER and record EVERY attempt, failures too:
1  device: the local drive / OneDrive through the device bridge (device_stage_files)
2  m365: the Microsoft 365 connector (SharePoint/OneDrive search, or the Teams transcript itself)
3  zapier: the Zapier Office 365 tools
Record each try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --need transcript --route device|m365|zapier --tool <tool you used> --result ok|fail --detail "<what happened>"
If Paul attached the file, use --route user. If another skill passed it in, use --route passed. Either with --result ok.

You may say a file cannot be reached ONLY after all three routes failed and are logged. Then record the question with: python3 {scripts}/run.py ask {run} --need <what you need> --question "<what you need from Paul>" --searched "<where you looked>" . It prints the exact words to give Paul. Never just say 'I cannot access your files'.
For a WhatsApp call there is no transcript file: ask Paul for his recap, notes or recording, confirm the exact date and TIME of the call, and log it with --route user.
steps.proof: the access log has an ok entry for 'transcript'

steps.title: Prepare and check the transcript is complete
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/tx.py prep <path to the transcript file> {run}
For a WhatsApp call whose source is a recap, notes or a recording summary with no timestamps, add --notes (the program then cannot check completeness, so tell Paul that).

If it prints STOP, tell Paul exactly what is missing and stop. If it says it could not read any timestamps, send Paul the first 15 lines of the file so the reader can be fixed. Use --force only if Paul says to carry on.
steps.proof: state.json exists and the transcript is complete (or forced on Paul's say-so)

steps.title: Read the client's file
do: Read, from the client's own file, everything below, and record each document you read:
python3 {scripts}/run.py source {run} --kind <kind> --path "<full path>" --date YYYY-MM-DD --read yes --ref "<short name>" --text-file <text copy>

Make a text copy of each document so the program can check your quotes and figures later: for a PDF run pdftotext "<file>" /tmp/<short name>.txt ; for an email or a page, save its text to a file. A document with no text copy is flagged to Paul at the end.

Kinds: Fact Find, Fact Find Summary, Earlier Note (every earlier Follow-Up Notes / WhatsApp summary), Overview (the latest), Quote (every Comparative Quotes folder of a current transaction), Application (every current transaction), Correspondence (Outlook, current transactions only).

If a kind has nothing on file, search it on at least two routes, log each search (run.py access --need <kind> --route device|m365|zapier --tool <tool> --result fail --detail "nothing found in <where>"), and only then: python3 {scripts}/run.py source {run} --kind <kind> --none "searched <where>, none found"
Use the access routes in order (device, m365, zapier) for every file and log failures with run.py access. Ask Paul ONLY for what no file holds, with run.py ask.
steps.proof: every kind of client-file source is read, or has a recorded reason

steps.title: Pass 1: read everything, in order, and keep the ledger
do: Read every chunk in order. The program will not serve chunk 2 before chunk 1, and it will not serve the next chunk until this one has ledger entries or a reasoned acknowledgement.
{chunk_commands_pass1}
AFTER EACH CHUNK, record every decision, acceptance, refusal, change of mind, correction, new fact, figure, and every request, instruction or offer either person makes:
python3 {scripts}/run.py ledger {run} add --line <line number> --kind <kind> --quote "<the exact words>" [--speaker Paul|Client] [--meaning "<in your words>"]
Kinds: decision, change, request, instruction, offer, acceptance, refusal, hold, fact, figure.

If a chunk really holds nothing to record, say so in your own words: python3 {scripts}/run.py ledger {run} ack --pass 1 --chunk <n> --reason "<what the chunk contained and why nothing needs recording>"
The program checks your quote against the transcript the moment you add it. A wrong quote is refused.
steps.proof: every chunk served in order, and ledger entries recorded

steps.title: Pass 2: read everything again
do: Read the WHOLE transcript a second time, chunk by chunk. Check every ledger entry against the actual words. Add anything Pass 1 missed (same ledger add command), above all in the closing minutes, the client's questions, anything the client asks Paul or Sitamah to do, offers Paul makes, items left 'for now', and every figure and name.
{chunk_commands_pass2}

After each chunk, add what you missed, or acknowledge it: python3 {scripts}/run.py ledger {run} ack --pass 2 --chunk <n> --reason "checked every entry in this chunk against the words; <what you checked>"
A keyword scan does not count as a read, and neither does re-reading only the parts that look important.
steps.proof: Pass 2 served every chunk in order

steps.title: Keyword scan
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/tx.py scan {run}

EVERY line marked * (a decision, change or request word) needs a ledger entry within 3 lines of it, or a recorded review: python3 {scripts}/run.py ledger {run} review --line <n> --reason "<why nothing was decided here>"   (for a stretch of plain chatter: --from <a> --to <b>). Lines marked C are in the closing minutes. Dismissals are counted and shown to Paul at the end.

steps.title: Write content.json (the one source for every output)
do: Write {run}/content.json. Model: {skill_dir}/references/content-example.json. `areas` is a LIST of {"key": ..., "bullets": [...]}. Every bullet and every action carries its source: a transcript line plus the exact words (at least 10 characters), or a document you recorded in the context step (cite its --ref and the exact words). Every figure in an item (money, quote or policy number, percentage) must appear in one of its sources.

TWO LENGTHS, ONE SET OF FACTS (Paul: the Planner note must be short). Every bullet has a `text`: the PDF line, at most 45 words. The 1 to 3 most important bullets of each area ALSO have a `short`: the Planner one-liner, one line, at most 20 words. The PDF shows at most 4 bullets per area and must fit two pages; the Planner note shows only the `short` lines. Merge bullets: one bullet can cite several sources. Each application also needs a `short`. Quote numbers, premiums and the status word go in the one-liner; the rest of the detail stays in the PDF or is left to the Overview and the quotes.

EVERY ACTION SAYS WHEN. `"when": "now"` = Sitamah can do it today. `"when": "later"` = it waits for something, named in `"trigger"` (for example "once the policy is issued"). Only the 'now' actions go in the Planner note and the PDF's Action Points; the 'later' ones go in the PDF under Coming up. NEVER write these as actions (Paul's rule): what the client decides (report it as PENDING - client deciding); cancelling credit life; sending quotes, proposals or the what's-next email, and setting up the next meeting (other steps of the pipeline do those); Paul's own steps. The ONLY credit-life action is: Sitamah to get the credit-life details from the client (when now). A cession is a 'later' action (once the policy is issued). `next_steps` lists only what the CLIENT must do, each with "owner": "client".
Answer EVERY item in the `checks` block (correspondence, owner change, cession, credit life, applications, quotes). None may be left out, and each is cross-checked against your text.

In every run (Teams meeting or WhatsApp call) also set `client_status` ("Review Client" or "Prospect") and `client_status_basis` (the folder path it comes from): a client in Company - WR Clients\Paul Kafentzis (Client Files) is a Review Client; a client in Company - Paul\New Business is a Prospect. If it is unclear, ask Paul with run.py ask. Never guess. Also `appointment_number` and its basis: the Teams meetings on file with this client plus this one; for a WhatsApp call, every meeting and call on file plus this one.

Then link every ledger entry to the items that cover it: python3 {scripts}/run.py ledger {run} cover <ledger id> <item id> [<item id> ...]   (or: ledger exclude <id> "reason" for a plain fact or figure). The covering item must cite the transcript close to that ledger line.
Check: python3 {scripts}/verify.py {run} --stage pre   and fix every FAIL before moving on.

steps.title: Build the outputs
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/build.py {run}

It builds the Planner page, the fallback text, the PDF (follow-up and WhatsApp only) and the message to Sitamah from content.json. If it refuses, fix what it says. Never hand-write any of these outputs.
steps.proof: outputs built from the current content.json

steps.title: Check the drafted outputs
do: 1. (Follow-up and WhatsApp) Open every page image in {run}/out (page-1.png, page-2.png ...) and look at them: each area its own bold heading, bullets with hanging indent, nothing cut off, no heading alone at the bottom of a page.

2. A second reader re-checks the key facts: give a subagent (Agent tool) ONLY the transcript and the drafted outputs and ask it to find any wrong person, figure, date, status, invented item or missed request. Required when the meeting has an acceptance, a change of owner/beneficiary/payer, or money amounts. If the Agent tool is not available, say so.

3. Answer in one sentence each (see the table above): were quotes named with insurer, type, number and premium; was every benefit explained from the actual quote; is nothing marked 'to confirm' that is on file; are independent actions worded as independent; was every garbled line flagged to Paul and not turned into a fact.

Record: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} --set png_visual_check="<what you saw on each page; not needed for a first meeting>" --set independent_check="subagent: <what it re-checked and found>" --set judgment.quotes_named="..." --set judgment.benefits_from_quote="..." --set judgment.nothing_to_confirm_on_file="..." --set judgment.independent_actions="..." --set judgment.garbled_flagged="..."
Fix anything found in content.json, rebuild with build.py, and check again.
steps.proof: the page images looked at, the independent re-check and the judgment items recorded

steps.title: Show the Planner note as a copy-ready page
do: Do NOT end your reply here and do not ask Paul anything yet: Paul is asked ONCE, at the last step, about all three outputs together (the Planner page, the PDF and the message to Sitamah). Record this step and go straight on with `run.py next`.

Publish {run}/out/planner_note.html as a private page with the Artifact tool (file_path = that file, do not retype it). Tell Paul in one sentence what the page is. After any correction, rebuild and republish the same page.
If the page tool is unavailable: say so, show {run}/out/planner_note.txt as formatted chat text (never in a code block), and state that this is the fallback.
Record it: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} --set planner_page.mode=artifact --set planner_page.url=<the link returned>
or the fallback: --set planner_page.mode=fallback_text --set planner_page.reason="<why the page tool was unavailable>"
steps.proof: planner_page recorded with the returned link

steps.title: Send, save and check the PDF
do: Do NOT end your reply here and do not ask Paul anything yet: Paul is asked ONCE, at the last step, about all three outputs together (the Planner page, the PDF and the message to Sitamah). Record this step and go straight on with `run.py next`.

1. If the folder /mnt/user-data/outputs exists, copy the PDF there first so it can be presented: cp "{run}/out/<the PDF file>" /mnt/user-data/outputs/ . Then send it in the chat for Paul to download (present_files / SendUserFile).
2. Save the same file into the client's 2. Fact Find folder with device_commit_files (route order as always).
3. List the folder back and confirm the new file's exact name, size and time.

Record it: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} --set pdf_sent_in_chat=true --set saved.tool=device_commit_files --set saved.folder="<folder>" --set saved.filename="<exact file name>" --set saved.tool_result="<tool result>" --set saved.folder_listing_check="<the listing line showing the file>"
steps.proof: PDF sent, saved and listed back, with the real tool output recorded

steps.title: Hand-offs: applications and revised quotes
do: Do NOT end your reply here and do not ask Paul anything yet: Paul is asked ONCE, at the last step, about all three outputs together (the Planner page, the PDF and the message to Sitamah). Record this step and go straight on with `run.py next`.
If applications differ from the meeting (the Applications section), call complete-applications-skill in Correction / Sync mode. If anything is unclear, ask Paul BEFORE any change.

If an owner or life assured changed, prepare the revised-quote email as a DRAFT and show Paul. Never send without his yes. Record what you showed: --set revised_quote_draft="shown to Paul: <what, when>"
Record: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} --set applications_handoff="complete-applications-skill called: <result>"   (or "n/a: <reason>")
Then suggest, without doing them: wr-roa-builder if a risk quote was accepted; teams-meeting-setup-skill if a new appointment was agreed.

steps.title: Show Paul everything and ask once; send the message to Sitamah only with his yes
do: {teams_message_block}

NOW WRITE YOUR REPLY TO PAUL. It holds all three outputs together: (1) the link to the Planner page, (2) the PDF, sent in the chat, (3) the exact message to Sitamah shown above, with the one-line check of why the follow-up sentence is in or out. End the reply with ONE question: "Shall I post this message to Sitamah in Teams?". Paul approves the page, the PDF and the message together. Then wait for his answer. Never end a reply without the message in it.

After his answer: if he says yes, send it exactly as shown, through Zapier only. Never send without his yes. Never twice for the same meeting. A correction does not trigger a resend unless Paul asks. Then record the result (sent, already_sent, declined or failed) with the receipt command shown above, including Paul's own words.
steps.proof: teams.status recorded as sent, declined or failed, with its evidence

steps.title: Final check
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/verify.py {run}

Your reply to Paul MUST contain its whole printout, unedited, including 'WHAT PAUL SHOULD GLANCE AT' and the DELIVERY LINE. If RESULT says FAIL you may not say the job is finished: say what failed and fix it first.
Then close the run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final

After ANY correction from Paul: edit content.json, run build.py again (it re-opens the hand-over steps), redo them for every output that changed, and run verify.py again. A correction re-opens the whole task.
